Name: Super Cleaning
Description:
[h2]Super Cleaning[/h2]

Ever watched a ship survive a fire, boarding action, and repair crisis only to discover that the real final boss was several thousand dirt marks? Well, have I got an aggressively organized mop queue for you!

Super Cleaning helps serious dirt backlogs keep moving. It starts Stardeus's normal floor-cleaning sweep when an otherwise available Cleaning Bot is idle, adds a bounded manual cleanup queue, and can optionally invite eligible Colonists to help before the first Cleaning Bot comes online. It does not delete dirt, replace worker AI, or interrupt work already in progress.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]Idle Cleaning Bot Assistance[/h3]
- Starts the vanilla floor-cleaning sweep when an otherwise available Cleaning Bot is idle and reachable dirt remains
- Honors Auto Clean, Cleaning job availability, direct control, work capability, safety, reservation, and reachability rules
- Leaves Bots undergoing maintenance, repairs, recharging, socializing, or other work alone
- Provides an independent Idle Assist toggle
- Idle Assist uses the Clean Now sweep, which may exceed any finite Bot Dock Work Radius > Range; ∞ is already unrestricted, while normal dock-assigned tasks still obey Range
- Lists idle Cleaning Bots in an expandable panel with the reason each one is waiting
- Lets you select and focus an idle Bot directly from that list

[h3]Bounded Cleanup Queue[/h3]
- Creates ordinary Stardeus floor-cleaning tasks for eligible deployed Cleaning Bots
- Requests 10% of the current dirt-mark count per click, with a minimum request of 24 when enough dirt exists
- Avoids positions that already have active floor-cleaning tasks
- Allows Stardeus to choose the worker, route, bidding, and completion behavior normally
- Tracks Super Cleaning tasks separately from vanilla and player-created cleaning tasks
- Can cancel pending Super Cleaning tasks without touching accepted, in-progress, vanilla, or player-created work

[h3]Colonist Assisted Early-Game Cleanup[/h3]
- Optional and disabled by default
- Adds a separate manual queue button for eligible Colonists and other non-Cleaning Bot workers with the Cleaning job available
- Uses ordinary task bidding rather than force-assigning anyone
- Does not enable jobs, interrupt current work, or turn Colonists into automatic cleaners

[h3]Cleaning Dashboard[/h3]
- Displays current dirt marks and all queued floor-cleaning tasks
- Separates vanilla/player and Super Cleaning queue totals
- Shows Cleaning Bots working, socializing, maintaining or recharging, idle, and performing other dynamically listed tasks
- Reports every Bot value as a count out of the total Cleaning Bot population
- Tracks the net dirt change over the last hour with expandable 10-minute sample history
- Keeps the detailed mod-owned task list collapsed until you want to inspect it
- Uses theme-aware tabs and disclosure controls that follow the active Stardeus UI theme

[h2]Important Behavior[/h2]

Super Cleaning creates normal Stardeus work; it does not guarantee that a task can begin or finish. Unsafe, unreachable, reserved, or otherwise unavailable dirt remains subject to Core's normal rules. A requested batch may also create fewer tasks when multiple dirt marks occupy the same floor tile or suitable workers cannot reach enough distinct targets.

Queue totals include tasks waiting for Core to retry or resume them. Super Cleaning retains ownership through temporary failures and interruptions, including across save/load. Ownership ends when Core removes the task or it enters a completed, cancelled, or terminal error state. Ownership already lost by older builds cannot be recovered reliably, so existing vanilla/player tasks are not relabeled.

Stardeus exposes a dirt mark's appearance and position but not the event that created it. The dashboard therefore reports measured net changes instead of guessing whether a footprint, fire, injury, toilet, battle, or something more creatively catastrophic caused the mess.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]

Requires [b]Stardeus 0.15.0[/b] and [b]Auto Utilities Mod Framework 1.4.0[/b]. AUMF provides the cooperative top-bar widget, managed resizable panel, compatibility handshake, theme-aware tabs, and collapsible sections used by this release. The AUMF DLL remains a separate dependency and is not bundled with Super Cleaning.

[h2]In Short[/h2]

You make the mess. Stardeus chooses who grabs the mop. Super Cleaning keeps the work visible and moving.

[b]One ship. Thousands of dirt marks. An aggressively supervised cleaning schedule.[/b]
